bull.b: Very low leverage gives Compass greater flexibility while it funds clinical development and absorbs operating losses. Limited debt reduces refinancing pressure and interest-related constraints, allowing more capital to remain available for research, trials, and other strategic priorities.

Positive Phase 2/3 efficacy results provide clinical support for tovecimig and strengthen the potential value of Compass’s lead program. Demonstrated improvements in response and progression-free survival may support future regulatory engagement and commercial development if remaining hurdles are addressed.

A proprietary antibody platform and advancing pipeline give Compass an opportunity to build value beyond a single clinical asset. Continued development across preclinical and clinical programs can create multiple shots on goal and preserve strategic optionality in oncology and other diseases.

bear.b: Deepening losses and negative operating results show that Compass has not yet developed a meaningful earnings base. Persistent unprofitability can consume capital, increase dependence on financing, and make future progress increasingly reliant on successful clinical and regulatory execution.

Material cash outflows reduce the resources available to advance clinical programs and sustain operations. The increase in free-cash-flow burn versus 2025 raises the likelihood that Compass will need additional financing over time, creating funding and potential dilution pressure.

The FDA’s request for an additional trial could extend the path toward a biologics application and require further spending before tovecimig can advance. Separately, Nasdaq compliance pressure introduces a possible delisting or reverse-split outcome, adding structural execution risk.
